_doc: doc 09 §2.14 / §8.3 — the teaching curriculum. One row per city level of doc 09 §2.11's ladder above the founding level, in play order. Read by `sim/progression/goal_system.gd`; every objective kind in it is a small pure evaluator in that file's EVENT_KINDS / STATE_KINDS tables, and a row naming a kind that file does not know is DROPPED at parse rather than crashing a city.
_ruling: Objectives ADVANCE the level; they do not gate it (doc 93 §G1). `city_level = max(population_ladder, objectives_earned)`, so the doc 92 §19 population rungs stay underneath as a backstop for a player who ignores the sheet — and for every scripted agent in `tools/playtest.gd`, which is why the balance matrix still measures the ladder it was fitted on.
_verbs: EVERY objective below is reachable from a surface the player can actually touch today: the build sheet (`cmd_place_building`, `cmd_place_grid_component`, `cmd_place_water_component`), its ROADS tab and the drag-path tool (`cmd_place_road` / `cmd_upgrade_road` / `cmd_demolish_road` / `cmd_place_water_main`, doc 12 §2.7), the building panel (`cmd_upgrade_building`) and its actions row (`cmd_repair_building` / `cmd_set_priority` / `cmd_demolish_building`, doc 12 §2.9 item 6), the land panel (`cmd_buy_block` / `cmd_start_development`), the dashboard's tax slider (`cmd_set_tax_level`) and the incident drawer (`cmd_dispatch_unit`). Wave 10 opened the last three doors doc 92 §17.6 recorded as missing, so `stamp_road_tiles` and `repair_buildings` are authorable and are used below. `place_water_main` is reachable but deliberately UNUSED: doc 05 §6 already runs a service lateral for every placed pump, so a main objective would teach reach the curriculum city does not yet need — see doc 93 §G4. `tests/test_goals_system.gd` holds this file to the reachable set.
_pacing: Targets are FITTED against the `curriculum` agent — a competent player who does the taught task and otherwise plays like `balanced`. One game-hour is one real minute at 1x (`SimHost.GAME_MS_PER_REAL_MS` = 60), so the measured durations ARE the session beat. RE-MEASURED for the Wave-9 re-arc + the level-6 rung on the merged tree (doc 92 §25.3 / §24.9, instrument `tools/measure_curriculum.gd`, seeds 1337/4242/9001, 45 game-days): see gate 21 for the held bounds. The two street/repair rows land on levels 3 and 4 (level 3 pays $7,200 of street on a thin treasury); level 6 is a saving beat for a $73,572 upgrade with a copper purchase in the middle of it (doc 92 §24.8). Retuning a target here is a BALANCE change: measure it with the `curriculum` agent and re-derive doc 92 §25.3 before you move it, and `tests/test_balance_gates.gd` gate 21 is what holds you to it — gate 21's horizon is 45 game-days since the sixth rung, because a six-level arc no longer fits in three game-weeks.

levels._added: doc 92 §24.7 (the level 5/6 content wave). Doc 92 §22.7 recorded why there was no sixth row: 'the ladder has five rungs above the founding level and a sixth would unlock nothing'. There is something to unlock now — doc 02 §2.14's tower tier — so the row exists, and the three objectives are the three halves of it: the rung, the archetype that was unlocked at city level 3 and that no earlier level ever mentions, and the capacity it all buys.

doc 92 §61 (Wave 22, the reward wave), and the player asked for it in these words on 2026-09-04: "we can even make a SEVENTH level where it's pretty much get a lot of buildings upgraded — get one of each type of building upgraded — and you get the big money when you go through the last level. That'll be five million." The rung is the whole city, audited: twelve rows, one per archetype `data/buildings.json` ships, each asking for ONE upgrade of that type. It is the last level and it is a CAPITAL level, so it is the only row in this file with no `reach_population` objective — doc 09 §2.14.2 says why, and `data/progression.json`'s rung 7 (40,500) is still underneath as the backstop the goals sheet greys out.
levels._archetype_scope: ALL TWELVE, civic and utility included, and the reason is the build sheet's own roster: `BuildController.cards()` walks `sim.catalog.archetypes()` with no filter, so every one of these twelve is a card the player can tap, every one has a priced upgrade ladder in `data/building_economy.json`, and `cmd_upgrade_building` accepts every one. Excluding the stations and the works would have made the graduation a residential-and-commercial exercise — and doc 03 §2.12 has been billing the player for `departments` and `fleet` since game-hour 1, so upgrading the station you have been paying for since founding is the curriculum closing its own loop. It is also what makes the level TEACHABLE rather than a wall: `data/starter_city.json` stands ten of the twelve up on the founding day, so ten rows are 'upgrade what you were given' and only `high_rise` (built at level 6) and `data_center` (the one archetype no earlier level ever mentions) have to be built first.
levels._the_ask: $644,370 at list price, and that is the number `data/economy.json`'s rung-6 grant is derived against: a data centre ($180,000) plus one L1→L2 step of each of the twelve — house 1,380 · store 2,990 · apartment 8,050 · office 14,950 · high_rise 29,900 · data_center 207,000 · police_station 20,700 · fire_station 23,000 · power_facility 69,000 · substation 17,250 · water_facility 51,750 · construction_yard 18,400 = 464,370. The rung-6 grant pays HALF of it ($325,000), which is doc 03 §2.5a's own rule and the reason the capstone is not prepaid: a grant that bought the chapter outright would delete it.
